props.title: Reuse interactions and page structures
props.lead: Components let you reuse a visual or interaction; templates let you reuse a page structure. Learn how to find them, insert them, adjust their settings, and manage changes between versions.

content.text: What do components and templates do?

values.component: How to draw data and how readers operate it
values.template: How to organize the content and what to write in each part

content.text: Find and insert the component

steps.title: Open the component library
steps.body: Go to "Components" in the left column. Filter by "Type": text, pictures, tables, data, processes, pages and whiteboards, others; you can also use the "Search Component" directly.
steps.note: "Scope" determines which sources of components to look at, and "Show all versions" lists historical versions of the same component.

steps.title: See the details before deciding
steps.body: Click on a component and there are three tabs for details: "Preview" shows real-time effects and examples, "Instructions" talks about applicable content and interactions, and "Parameters" lists adjustable inputs, types and default values.

steps.title: insert page
steps.body: First open a page, then click "Insert Page" in the upper right corner of the details. The currently selected sample data will be inserted together. The faster way to write is to enter `/`in the text and search for the component name directly.
steps.result: The component appears on the page and can be edited.

steps.title: Adjust parameters
steps.body: Select the component and open its settings. The title, height, font size, color palette, legend and interactive switches of the chart can be changed; the data and fields correspond to "Data and Advanced Parameters". For custom components, use "Edit Component Data" to directly modify JSON, and it will be verified according to parameter rules before saving.
steps.note: If the data does not meet the parameter rules, it will not be saved, and the original page data will remain unchanged.

content.text: Basic table
Type

to search for “Table”, or insert one from the component library. Basic tables display all horizontal and vertical grid lines and an outer border by default. Borders are 1px wide and use the page theme color.

Click a header or cell to edit it. Hover over the table to set text alignment for the whole table, or over a header to align that column. Use “Add row” and “Remove last row” below the table to change the number of rows.
Where do components come from
The same component ID may exist in several places at the same time. Both the workbench and Agent are searched in a fixed order, and the references are locked to
Specific versions and content fingerprints

nodes.label: Components in the page
nodes.detail: Look around below for newer versions available in order as you insert. Complete `version `and `integrity `when saving, and always use this copy when opening the page.

nodes.label: project
nodes.detail: Versions created, imported, or derived from this project. It is only visible to this project and will not automatically appear in other projects. The write must specify a real project.

nodes.label: overall situation
nodes.detail: The user is **explicitly registered** to the local version globally. When registering, the sub-components and sub-templates it depends on will be copied together, so they are still available after deleting the source project. Registration will not upload anything.

nodes.label: Published
nodes.detail: The release package is downloaded from the actual statically hosted URL and verified byte by byte. Web pages that "reference published components" can then be exported.

nodes.label: built-in
nodes.detail: Components and templates released with ShowAI as a last resort. If you want to change a built-in component, first derive it into the project and save your own version.

nodes.label: Other items
nodes.detail: Forking from a global or released version to another project requires a new version number or a new name, and records the source `parents `. Modifying the derived version does not affect the original version.

props.caption: The same ID and version number can have different contents in different scopes, so the page recognizes "version + fingerprint", not just the name.

content.text: Versioning, forking and merging
Each version of components and templates
Cannot be rewritten
: In the same scope, an ID plus a version number only corresponds to one piece of content. If you want to make changes, save the new version; pages already using the old version will not be affected.

steps.label: Create value-slider 1.0.0
steps.detail: New components are always saved in a project first. The page locks 1.0.0 and its content fingerprint when inserting it.

steps.label: After modification, save it as 1.1.0
steps.detail: If the content changes, the version number must be changed. Pages that have already been inserted into 1.0.0 continue to use 1.0.0.

steps.label: Explicitly register to global
steps.detail: Registration is an explicit operation, and the target must be specified as global. Dependent sub-components and sub-templates are written first, and the root version is written last; if there is a global version with the same name and the same version but different content, the entire registration will report a conflict before writing.

steps.label: Derived from 2.0.0
steps.detail: The fork requires a new version number or a new name, and records the source in parents . Derived components require readable source code.

steps.label: Modify both sides separately
steps.detail: Both Project A and Project B have made different modifications based on the original version and need to be merged together.

steps.label: Three-party merger preview
steps.detail: Provide three locking references: base (common source), ours, and theirs. JSON is merged field by field, and source code is merged line by line; different changes in the same place return conflicting positions and three-sided content. The preview is not written to the directory.

steps.label: Save as new version after resolving conflicts
steps.detail: When saving, check the three references again, create a version of the project and record parents: [ours, theirs] and mergeBase. Any parent version will not be overwritten.

content.text: In the workbench you mainly do browsing, previewing and inserting. The operations of creating, importing, deriving, merging, and registering are completed by Agent or CLI:

rows.label: Browse and preview components and templates
Create a new page using a template
Register to the local machine globally
rows.hint: The MCP of the bound project cannot write to the shared directory

props.note: Just let the Agent directly describe the requirements when doing it, such as "derive a copy of this slider component and add unit selection." For the division of skills, see [Skills and Workflow] (https://showai.renaissancemind.ai/doc/skills).

content.text: The following command needs to first quote the exact reference in the directory result (
kind
id
version
integrity
) is saved as a JSON file. For full instructions see
CLI & MCP Reference

showai catalog import --project PROJECT --input ./component-package --json
showai catalog fork --project PROJECT --input ref.json --id my-variant --version 1.0.0 --json
showai catalog promote --project PROJECT --input ref.json --to global --json
showai catalog merge preview --project PROJECT --input merge-input.json --out merge-preview.json --json
showai catalog merge resolve --project PROJECT --input resolved-merge.json --json
Start a page with a template

When creating a new page, in addition to "Page" and "Board", the dialog box will also list templates with page skeletons. You can browse by type in the "Template" on the left column. Details include "Preview", "Usage Instructions" and "Stage Guide".

cards.title: Concept and mechanism explanation
cards.body: Starting from specific problems, establishing objects, relationships, mechanisms and applicable boundaries can be explained from shallow to deep.

cards.title: Plan comparison and decision-making
cards.body: Present comparable facts, missing items and trade-offs according to common standards, and support conditional choices.

cards.title: Research and evidence reporting
cards.body: Organize facts, evidence, and limitations around the research question, distinguishing source claims from analytical inferences.

cards.title: Operation and troubleshooting

cards.title: Status and progress reports
cards.body: Describe the current status, changes, evidence, risks and next steps with clear deadlines.

cards.title: Exploration and data organization
cards.body: Organize data with positionable categories, attributes and relationships, supporting overview, filtering and partial verification.

content.text: The earlier "Blank Canvas", "Research", "Comparison" and "Presentation" templates are still available.
Templates are more than just skeletons

Each of these six templates comes with a staged writing guide: reader goals, evidence materials, understanding path, visual design, page production, and review and improvement. When Agent writes a page using a template, it will read the corresponding guide at each stage and then fill it in with your real materials.

Templates don't automatically bind data or do research for you. When materials are missing, the completed page retains the missing items and conclusion constraints instead of leaving an unprocessed fill-in prompt.
What you get after applying the template is
independent page
: After the template is updated, the existing page will not change; the template itself is not needed to read this page.

attrs.title: Templates can be combined with other templates

content.text: A template can reference sub-templates in sequence, expand recursively when expanded, and insert secondary titles before sub-templates. Circular references and missing dependencies are checked before expansion; the nesting depth is up to 16 levels and up to 12,000 nodes after expansion.

When a combined template is registered globally, the subtemplates and custom components used by it will be copied together, and can still be expanded even after changing a device or deleting the source project.
If you want to refine a written page into a template, or make a template folder with guidelines and component libraries for your team, see
Develop Custom Components
